actual_use_paragraphs:
Suppose the uniform all-fibre-open cohomological dimension bound of
[[lem-finite-fibre-dimension-gives-bounded-fibrewise-soft-resolutions]] holds,
and choose its finite resolution $k_X\to K$; for an open $U\subseteq X$ put
$K_U=j_{U!}j_U^*K$ ([[def-extension-by-zero-abelian-sheaf]],
[[def-c-soft-sheaf]]). For a bounded-below injective complex $I$ on $Y$,
define the exceptional inverse-image candidate to be the sheaf complex with
open sections $\operatorname{Hom}_Y^\bullet(f_!K_U,I)$.
[[thm-compactly-supported-derived-pushforward-has-exceptional-inverse-image-adjoint]]
proves that this candidate is a sheaf complex and is independent of the chosen
resolution. Set $\omega_X=a_X^!k$ and $D_XA=R\mathcal Hom(A,\omega_X)$ when the
terminal map satisfies the same finite-dimensional hypotheses. Constructible
restriction is a separate geometric theorem; none of these definitions asserts
a generic six-functor axiom.
direct_use_rows.applicability: The consumer explicitly carries the uniform bound over all sheaves on all opens of fibres and uses a finite resolution of a sheaf, in particular k_X. The adjunction theorem F7 expressly excludes unsupported bounded-complex compatible resolutions; the bounded-source scope and LCH hypotheses agree with the supplier.

actual_use_paragraphs: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and the uniform all-fibre-open dimension bound $d$ of [[lem-finite-fibre-dimension-gives-bounded-fibrewise-soft-resolutions]]. For a continuous map $f:X\to Y$ of locally compact Hausdorff spaces, the proper-support functor $f_!$ of [[def-derived-operations-on-analytic-sheaves-over-locally-compact-spaces]] is left exact, satisfies $(Rf_!A)_y\simeq R\Gamma_c(X_y,A|_{X_y})$ on every fibre, and maps bounded derived categories into bounded derived categories. Its exceptional inverse-image candidate $f^!$ represents the natural Hom transposition $$\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_!A,B)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(A,f^!B)$$ for bounded source objects $A$ and bounded-below target objects $B$, and has lower cohomological bound $\inf(B)-d$. When the later geometric theorem proves that $f^!$ preserves the bounded constructible subcategory, this becomes the right adjunction $Rf_!\dashv f^!$ there; on that bounded constructible specialization the adjunction unit, counit and resolution comparisons satisfy the triangle, identity and cocycle laws. The proper-support evaluation constructs the counit directly. The proof constructs this adjoint from a finite fibrewise-soft resolution and generator complexes, independently of Verdier biduality; it does not infer an unrestricted $D^+$-source adjunction from the bounded-source generator argument.

[F7] The uniform all-fibre-open bound $d$ gives every $k$-sheaf on $X$ a bounded resolution $0\to\mathcal A\to\mathcal K^0\to\dots\to\mathcal K^d\to0$ whose terms are $c$-soft on every fibre, the constant sheaf in particular has such a resolution; the supplier does not assert a bounded-complex compatible resolution, and none is needed below ([[lem-finite-fibre-dimension-gives-bounded-fibrewise-soft-resolutions]]).

actual_use_paragraphs: **Given:** The Axiom of Choice; a smooth quasiprojective complex variety $U$ of pure dimension $d$; an SNC smooth projective compactification $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ with reduced boundary $D$ a simple normal crossings divisor ([[def-simple-normal-crossings-divisors]], [[lem-smooth-quasiprojective-varieties-admit-snc-projective-compactifications]]); the irreducible components $D_1,\dots,D_r$ of $D$ and, for $a\ge0$, the smooth projective scheme $D^{[a]}$ equal to $X$ for $a=0$ and to the disjoint union of the $a$-fold intersections $D_{i_1}\cap\dots\cap D_{i_a}$ for $a\ge1$, with its natural map $i_a:D^{[a]}\to X$ (each summand maps by a closed immersion; the disjoint union need not embed in $X$). Cohomology is singular cohomology of the analytic spaces on the analytic topology of [[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]].

[F7] Compactification and modification ([[lem-smooth-quasiprojective-varieties-admit-snc-projective-compactifications]], [[lem-smooth-projective-modification-preserves-open-cohomology-images]]). Any finite family of smooth projective compactifications of $U$ is dominated by a smooth projective compactification with reduced SNC boundary restricting to the identity over $U$; a proper morphism of smooth projective varieties of equal pure dimension that is the identity over $U$ does not change the image of $H^n(-;\mathbb Q)$ in $H^n(U;\mathbb Q)$.
